summary: As part of the project, we developed an interactive application and a model based on NASA satellite data and machine learning that predict crop yields and soil quality at specified coordinates. This tool solves the problem of crop selection by automatically simulating crop rotation and selecting the best plant combinations without the need to rely on the complex expertise of agronomists. This is important because it makes remote land analysis and crop planning simple and accessible even for beginners.
details:
The tool converts a single point on the map into a multi-year crop rotation plan. The user selects a location on the map or enters coordinates; the tool collects publicly available climate and soil data for that point, assesses the suitability of each crop, and generates a crop rotation plan consisting of five crops. The most suitable crop comes first, followed by crops that are also suitable for this soil and can be planted after the previous one according to agronomic crop rotation rules.

Farmers receive a data-driven basis for crop selection and planning the next five growing seasons for any land area with data coverage. This does not require field sensors or paid data.

Tools: Python, Google Earth API, NASA POWER, Olsen P, ISRIC SoilGrids, Streamlit.
